name: Competitive form
construction: Average result points from the previous ten selected competitive internationals. Award 3 for a win, 1 for a draw and 0 for a loss, regardless of competition format.
reason: Summarises recent competitive success without requiring a large winning margin. Higher values for A are expected to favour A.
limitation: Points ignore the margin of victory and remain sensitive to opponent quality. A draw followed by a shootout win still earns one synthetic result point.

name: Clean sheet rate
construction: Fraction of the previous ten competitive matches in which the team conceded zero goals.
reason: Measures how often a defence completely prevents scoring. This can distinguish teams with similar average concession totals.
limitation: It discards the difference between conceding one and several goals. Opponents and tactical choices affect the rate.

name: Scoring failure rate
construction: Fraction of the previous ten competitive matches in which the team scored zero goals.
reason: Measures attacking reliability. A higher failure rate for A is expected to lower its goal difference.
limitation: A scoreless match can reflect poor finishing or strong opposition. This is an observed event rate, not shot-based expected goals.

name: Margin volatility
construction: Sample standard deviation of goals scored minus goals conceded over the previous ten competitive games, using n minus 1 in the variance denominator.
reason: Tests whether inconsistency adds information beyond form. Large wins and losses can distinguish unstable performance.
limitation: There is no definite expected coefficient sign. Volatility may affect uncertainty more than the expected margin, so this is deliberately an exploratory feature.

name: Form momentum
construction: Mean result points in the most recent five competitive games minus the mean in the preceding five. Then subtract the two teams' momentum values.
reason: Tests whether a recent improvement adds information beyond the ten-match average.
limitation: A short run can be random or reflect easier opponents. The feature shares information with competitive form; usefulness must be tested conditionally.

name: Past opponent strength
construction: For each of the ten previous competitive opponents, calculate its points per game in its own ten competitive games BEFORE that historical meeting. Average those ten opponent values.
reason: Adds context to the schedule behind a team's form. Similar results against stronger opponents may mean something different.
limitation: This is a simple schedule proxy, not an Elo rating or a complete strength adjustment. Strong teams in weak confederations can still have high points rates.

name: Recent workload
construction: Count all recorded internationals in the interval from 30 days before the prediction date up to, but excluding, that date. Include friendlies for this feature.
reason: Tests a scheduling and recovery hypothesis. More recent matches may mean more fatigue, but could also improve preparation.
limitation: The count does not measure player minutes, club workload, travel or rotation. Fixture-congestion evidence is mixed, and a 30-day count is a coarse proxy (Julian et al., 2021).

name: World Cup experience
construction: Count matches played in the 2014, 2018 and 2022 World Cups and apply the natural logarithm of one plus that count. Subtract B from A.
reason: Tests whether recent national-team tournament experience adds context. The logarithm limits the influence of highly experienced nations and handles zero appearances.
limitation: This measures national-team history, not the current players' experience. It also reflects prior qualification and strength; no causal interpretation is justified.
